text:
UN General Assembly resolutions are not a formal source of international law under Article 38(1) of the ICJ Statute, because they are generally non-binding recommendations. Their value is indirect: they can be evidence of opinio juris and so help establish or crystallise customary law (as in *Nicaragua* and *Nuclear Weapons*), and they can help interpret treaties. The team note is wrong: a resolution does not automatically codify custom or conclusively prove it, since the ICJ looks at the resolution's content, the conditions of its adoption, and whether State practice and opinio juris actually support it.

CONFIDENCE: 92
